severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — FOREIGN INTERFERENCE ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: STATE-SPONSORED SLOP FRONT DRIFTS ACROSS FIVE REGIONS AS INDUSTRIAL PROPAGANDA OPERATIONS ABANDON CRAFTSMANSHIP ENTIRELY AND SWITCH TO THE CHEAP STUFF, DEPLOYING BORROWED CELEBRITY FACES AND OFF-BRAND NEWSROOMS AT VOLUMES NO HUMAN PAYROLL COULD SUSTAIN
advisory: The Service is tracking a persistent high-volume system in which large influence operations have quietly downgraded from bespoke disinformation to bulk-generated slop, prioritizing quantity over plausibility. Residents are advised that a video is not a document, a face is not a source, and a confident anchor voice is not a newsroom. When in doubt, verify laterally: open a second, unrelated source before you open your wallet, your outrage, or your repost button. This is a mass-produced weather system operating on the same economics as everything else in the forecast — it is simply cheaper now to be wrong at scale.

regional_outlook.conditions: Gale-force reposting as generated clips of borrowed celebrity faces circulate faster than corrections. Visibility poor; source-of-source concealed behind a wall of quote-tweets.
Fog of near-identical 'independent news' pages, each citing the others in a closed loop. Ground truth reported somewhere beneath page four.
Steady inflow of dramatic minute-long video systems, newly capable of sustaining a false scene without collapsing into melted geometry. Residents advised to check timestamps against reality.
Rapid updrafts of synthetic breaking-news montages set to urgent orchestral swells. Ambient credibility artificially inflated by lower-thirds that mean nothing.
Rising tide of urgent forwards begging you to 'watch before it gets deleted.' Nothing is being deleted; everything is being generated.

specimen.status: Invasive; state-subsidized; multiplying faster than it can be catalogued
specimen.habitat: Freshly registered domains with authoritative-sounding names, cross-posted into the X Badlands and the Search Results Basin
specimen.field_marks: A confident masthead in a font that whispers 'trust me,' a masthead-anchor who never blinks in a way that reads correctly, and a story that appears nowhere a real newsroom would have run it. Bylines are plausible; the humans behind them are not.
specimen.call: BREAKING: sources confirm what you already suspected, share before they take this down
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for an actual small local news outlet. Distinguishing feature: a real newsroom has a phone number that a real person answers, a correction it once had to issue, and a staff that ages. This one was born fully grown at 9 a.m. and will be gone by Friday.

spotter_tip: If a shocking clip features a face you recognize saying something no one else on earth is reporting, treat the face as a costume, not a witness. Real events tend to leave more than one footprint.
tomorrow: Front lingers; expect scattered debunkings arriving several news cycles after the damage, as usual.

confirmed_sighting.report: Researchers at Graphika report that many of the largest state-sponsored online propaganda campaigns have adopted low-quality AI-generated content, including a pro-Russia deepfake video featuring an AI version of a Hollywood actor. The Service notes, without surprise, that even influence operations have discovered it is cheaper to generate the slop than to make it well.
